{"id": "a2bf2371-fb5c-4e34-9891-ad16daea3903", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's what I found:

**The general rule:** No, not by default. CloudTrail splits events into two categories:
- **Management events** (control-plane, e.g. `CreateBucket`, `UpdateFunctionConfiguration`) — logged by default on every trail.
- **Data events** (data-plane, e.g. S3 `DeleteObject`/`GetObject`/`PutObject`, Lambda `Invoke`) — **off by default**. You have to explicitly add them to a trail's event selectors, and they cost extra.

**What your trails actually show (account 012345678901_1):**

| Trail | Data events enabled? | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| `IsengardTrail-DO-NOT-DELETE` | No | Management events only (all read/write) |
| `nebula-single-region-trail` | No | Management events only (all read/write) |
| `nebula-data-events-trail` | Partial — S3 only | Data events scoped to **just one bucket**: `nebula-audit-covered-012345678901_1` |
| `JMERWIN_Org_Trail` | Unknown | This is an org trail owned by a different account (012345678901_2), so I couldn't pull its event selectors from here — it may add broader coverage if your account is a member of that org |

So concretely:
- **S3 object deletes** — only captured if the object lives in `nebula-audit-covered-012345678901_1`. A delete anywhere else won't show up as a CloudTrail data event on any trail I could inspect.
- **Lambda invokes** — not captured by any trail I could see in this account. No trail has a Lambda data event selector configured.

If you want full coverage, you'd need to add S3 and Lambda data event selectors to one of your trails (or confirm the org trail already covers it). Want me to look at what adding that coverage would involve?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
